exhaustive_review: Reviewed and re-executed: the template (index 0) always takes the minimum native size because randint(a, b if i else a). So 32 templates x 260 object variants (every shape/angle/width/height) cover the full per-object native domain; objects are separated by spacing 1, so each component is classified independently. Re-run here under all 8 D4 transforms with a shuffled palette (66560 solves), and cross-checked against an independently coded family form: 0 failures.

issues.issue: No callable ambiguity gate existed. coverage-repairs-v3 evidence.py takes a single query_input, only reports, and never raises. Added evidence_bd14c3bf.require_bd14c3bf_evidence(demonstrations, queries, palette=None, d4=None), which takes queries=[{"input": grid}].

Collapse-only and family (stroke-length) shape equivalence disagree when the template is a Y and an object is a 5-long Y. The old host counterexample (counterexample.json) is such a case: its demos do not show Y stretching, so the gate rejects it. Keeping the query and adding one native Y-template demo resolves it (test_old_counterexample_context_shortfall_then_resolved). Coarse topology (holes, ends) also merges C/L and H/P, and is likewise rejected until demos separate them.

The direct program ignores demonstrations; the rule is fixed with palette roles bg=palette[0], template=palette[2]. Its forms are D4-invariant, so d4 is unused, which is correct and not a hidden choice. There is no fallback output: with no template component the input is returned unchanged, and this never happens natively.

leakage_review: verify() executes solve in a fresh namespace with copied demos and query input only. The gate reads demo pairs and query inputs; the test proves that a bogus query "output" key does not change its result. Labels are compared only after prediction in the audit scripts.
intrinsic_ambiguity: None in the native domain. The exhaustive check shows that the native label of every object is a deterministic function of its visible shape and the visible template, so no identical-input / different-output witness exists. All observed gate rejections are context shortfalls resolved by redrawing demos for the same query.
